summary.text: Color vision is the ability to tell apart light of different frequencies, no matter how bright that light is.
It begins when three kinds of cone cells in the retina respond differently to incoming light, and the brain then combines their outputs.
Cones handle daylight, while rods handle dim light and add little to color, so very dim scenes give little color.

facts.label: Newton's prism result
facts.value: Split light recombined into white with a second prism

facts.label: Peak sensitivity
facts.value: Rods near 500 nm, cones near 555 nm

facts.label: Why primates see color
facts.value: Possibly to find ripe fruit and young leaves

items.prompt: You walk into a dark bedroom at night and can make out shapes, but everything looks gray. What best explains this?

options.label: Your cones switch to a special night mode that strips hue
Rod cells are doing the work, and they play little part in color
The pupil closes down, which removes color from the light
Objects lose their color whenever no sunlight falls on them

items.explain: In very dim light vision is carried by rods, which contribute little to color vision. Cones, which do color, need brighter light.

items.prompt: A friend says the long-wavelength cones in your eye are simply red detectors. What is wrong with that?

options.label: They actually respond only to blue light
They respond to every wavelength equally
Their peak sensitivity is in the greenish-yellow region
They only switch on in very dim light

items.explain: Measurements show the long cones peak in the greenish-yellow, so the cone types do not match red, green and blue directly.

items.prompt: A lighting designer wants just two colored lights that a viewer will see as white when combined. Which pair works for humans?

options.label: Blue and yellow
Red and orange
Green and cyan
Violet and blue

items.explain: White can be perceived from red, green and blue together, or from a pair of complementary colors such as blue and yellow.

items.prompt: A biologist asks why early monkeys might have gained an edge from seeing a wider range of hues. Which is the best fit?

options.label: It let them find prey in total darkness
It let them hear predators from farther away
It let them see through thick tree trunks
It helped them spot ripe fruit and tender young leaves

items.explain: In primates, color vision may have evolved under pressure to find nutritious young leaves, ripe fruit and flowers, and to notice camouflage and emotional states.

items.prompt: At dusk it is too dim for full daylight vision but not fully dark. What is the retina doing?

options.label: Only the rods send signals
Only the cones send signals
Both rods and cones send signals to the ganglion cells
Neither sends signals, and the brain fills in the scene

items.explain: Between dim-light and daylight vision lies mesopic vision, where both rods and cones feed the retinal ganglion cells.

items.prompt: Sunlight is split into colored bands by one prism, and the bands are then sent through a second prism. What does Newton's discovery predict comes out?

options.label: White light again
The same bands, spread even wider
A single band of green light
Darkness, because the colors cancel

items.explain: Newton found that the split colors can be recombined into white light by passing them through a different prism.
